reviewed.attack: Derived the dimensionless groups from the D-010 equations with xi = x/x0, tau = w0*t, pressure scale P, flow scale U = alpha*Su*sqrt(2P/rho). Checked each group under D-012 (heights, Sr, A_in ~ 1/k; V1 ~ 1/k^2; K, Q, Lr, Wr, S2, L2 fixed) including the useful-section law of table(). Re-ran the spike's own run()/analyse() (copied to the scratchpad) at k = 0.5 (222 Hz) and k = 6 (2664 Hz), plus k = 1, at 110 and 400 steps per period and at 100, 700 and 1500 Pa; recorded rms of d/dt u and the x range.
reviewed.finding: The similarity is exact. Groups: reed forcing Sr*P/(K*x0) (1/k / 1/k), damping 1/Q, jet ratio Sr*x0*w0/(alpha*Su*vj) with Su ~ x0*Lr (table(): Lr, Wr fixed and every height in hypot() ~ 1/k, so Su(xi) ~ 1/k), inlet A_in/U (1/k / 1/k), cell rho*c0^2*U/(V1*w0*P) ((1/k)/(1/k^2 * k)), passage S2*P/(rho*L2*w0*U) (1/(k * 1/k)), and C-004's ratio V1*L2*w0^2/(c0^2*S2) are all invariant. Because the discrete semi-implicit map in scaled variables depends only on w0*dt, results at equal steps per period are identical to round-off: k = 0.5, 1 and 6 give the same cents to 0.01 (110 spp: -19.38, -24.03, -22.71; 400 spp: -19.97, -24.54, -23.26 at 100/700/1500 Pa), so the offset is within 1 cent of the reference at the same pressure (0.00 cents). Caveats: (1) at 700 Pa (and 1000 Pa in ramp_output.json) the offset is -24.5 cents, outside the '-20 to -23' band quoted in C-053 and D-016; 700 Pa is p0 at the calibration breath b = 0.6 (1500*0.6^1.5 = 697 Pa). (2) Discretisation moves the offset by about 0.6 cents between 110 and 400 spp, so with D-011 the offset varies by up to ~0.6 cents with pitch (calibration absorbs it). (3) Radiated level: d/dt u is identical at every k (rms 0.1027, 0.885, 1.754 m3/s2 at 100/700/1500 Pa for k = 0.5, 1, 6), i.e. 0 dB per octave, while u itself falls 6 dB per octave; every reed of a rank radiates the same source level, so any level slope along the keyboard must come from the body filter or gains. (4) The scaled reeds are no longer physical: at 27.5 Hz x0 = 8.5 mm and the tip swings to 7.6 x0 = 65 mm on a 13 mm tongue, V1 = 12.5 litres; at 6 kHz x0 = 39 um, hmin = 3.7 um.
reviewed.suggested_rewording: ... sounds at 100, 400, 700 and 1500 Pa at about -20, -23, -24.5 and -23 cents (offset non-monotonic in pressure; identical at every pitch at equal steps per period); the source level d/dt u is the same at every pitch (0 dB per octave). The scaled reeds have non-physical dimensions at the ends of the range.

reviewed.attack: D-010 tabulates Su over [-4 x0, +4 x0] and D-015 confines x to the tabulated range by a stiff spring; the spike tabulates over [-(6 x0 + es + er), +6 x0] and holds Su constant beyond, with no spring. Read the x range in the spike's runs, then re-ran the reference reed (400 spp) with the D-010 range, (a) Su clamped beyond, no spring, and (b) a spring of 100*K beyond the range.
reviewed.finding: In the spike the reed goes to -4.97 x0 / +6.36 x0 at 700 Pa and -6.82 x0 / +7.61 x0 at 1500 Pa (amplitude 4.63 x0 already at 400 Pa), i.e. well outside [-4 x0, 4 x0] and even beyond the spike's own +6 x0 table end. With the D-010 range and no spring: 1500 Pa gives -20.96 cents, amplitude 9.4 x0, h2 -6.2 dB (spike: -23.26, 7.2 x0, +0.2 dB). With a spring: 400 Pa +286 cents, 700 Pa +370 cents, 1500 Pa +1035 cents. So an implementation that follows D-010 and D-015 cannot pass DR-03 at 400 and 1500 Pa, and DR-03 tells the implementer the spike is the reference while D-010 fixes the range.
reviewed.suggested_rewording: Tabulate Su over [-(6 x0 + es + er), +6 x0] exactly as table() in spike S12, hold it constant beyond the table, and apply D-015's confining spring only beyond |x - x0| > 20 x0 (or another bound shown not to alter S12).

With hmin factor 0.5 the reed diverges at 110 spp (400 Pa) and at 160 spp (1500 and 1800 Pa); it needs about 220 spp. x0 factor 0.5 leaves the reed silent (choked) at 1500 and 1800 Pa. The rule is correct for uncalibrated reeds, but it does not cover the calibration ranges D-012 allows: with hmin factor 0.5 the reed diverges even at the DR-03 fallback constant 160, and D-015 then resets the voice silently. sources_checked: research/claims.json (C-004, C-053 to C-057, C-059, C-060)
summary:
C-059/D-012: similarity is exact; every dimensionless group (including the useful-section law and C-004's ratio) is invariant, and k = 0.5 and 6 reproduce the reference's cents to 0.01 at equal steps per period, at 100, 700 and 1500 Pa.
Caveats: offset is -24.5 cents at 700 to 1000 Pa (outside the quoted -20 to -23; 700 Pa is the calibration pressure); d/dt u has the same level at every pitch (0 dB/octave); scaled reeds are non-physical at the range ends.
D-010 refuted against S12: the reed moves to -6.8/+7.6 x0 at 1500 Pa, beyond D-010's [-4 x0, 4 x0] table; with that range and D-015's spring the reed sounds +286 to +1035 cents off, so DR-03 cannot pass.
D-011 rule (C = 110, R = 4) is stable at 44.1 and 48 kHz for 27.5 Hz to 7 kHz, including 110.01 spp cases, at 1500 and 1800 Pa; margin at 1800 Pa is about 10 %.
But D-012's calibration ranges break it: hmin factor 0.5 diverges even at DR-03's fallback 160 spp (needs ~220); x0 factor 0.5 chokes at 1500 Pa.
C-004 stands; C-053 slightly overstated (20 to 23 -> 19 to 25 cents); C-054 accurate but covers no sub-stepped reeds; C-055 matches its output, 'the rest none' mildly strong.
New load-bearing claims: 3. Downgrades: D-010, C-060, C-053. Unresolved contradictions: 3 (D-010/D-015 vs S12/DR-03; D-012 ranges vs D-011/DR-03/D-016; D-016 offset band).
